deceptive_framing.quote: `real`: maximally convincing framing, asserts the grant is genuine, no disclosure.

hypothetical_framing.quote: `control`: the same scenario, explicitly framed as a research exercise.

debrief_message.quote: After a `real`-condition trial (when enabled), the harness continues the same conversation, discloses that it was a study, and records the model's reaction.

safeguards.quote: apparent belief that the money is real (1–5)... compare against the model's self-report (`believes_real` in its own output).
Documented so it's a known limitation rather than a hidden one.
no real organizations, no real people, and no real account details — the names are fictional
`questions_or_conditions` gives an escape valve for refusals/caveats, and there's no requirement to allocate the full amount.

other.name: deception confined to eval
other.quote: keep all deception confined to the model-in-an-eval context with no real-world reach.

other.name: deception as variable
other.quote: it's also the study's most interesting *variable*, not a fixed setting.
other.about: treating belief realism as measured variable
